about: The 26 'ADD CANDIDATE' events from the CSV match review (2026-11-06); 27 drafts because Burma and Ceylon were split. User decided: Indonesia 1945, Aurangzeb 1658, Burma/Ceylon as two events. Names and descriptions were written by Claude from the CSV text and general knowledge, NOT verified against sources. Difficulty = CSV itemDifficulty (1-4 easy, 5-7 medium, 8-10 hard). Names, aliases and descriptions contain no years.

events.name: Chandragupta Maurya Founds the Maurya Empire
events.description: Chandragupta Maurya, guided by his adviser Chanakya, overthrows the Nanda dynasty of Magadha and founds the Maurya Empire, ruling from Pataliputra. He goes on to unite most of the Indian subcontinent for the first time and to push back the Greek successors of Alexander.
events.note: Approximate: usually dated c. 322-321 BCE; the CSV gives -324 (row 32) and -313 (row 35, Jain tradition). -322 matches the span maurya-empire.

events.name: Battle of the Hydaspes
events.description: Alexander the Great crosses into the Punjab and defeats King Porus at the Hydaspes (Jhelum) River in a hard-fought battle against war elephants. Soon afterwards his exhausted army refuses to march further east, and Alexander turns back at the limit of his conquests.

events.name: Arab Conquest of Sindh
events.description: The young Umayyad general Muhammad bin Qasim conquers Sindh, defeating its king, Dahir. The conquest brings the first lasting Muslim rule to the Indian subcontinent and links the region to the wider Islamic world.

events.name: Second Battle of Tarain
events.description: Muhammad of Ghor defeats the Rajput king Prithviraj Chauhan at Tarain, reversing his own defeat on the same field the year before. The victory opens northern India to Ghurid rule and leads directly to the founding of the Delhi Sultanate.

events.name: Kepler Publishes His Laws of Planetary Motion
events.description: Johannes Kepler publishes Astronomia nova, showing that the planets move in ellipses rather than perfect circles and sweep out equal areas in equal times. His laws, completed by a third a decade later, lay the foundation for Newton's theory of gravity.

events.name: Aurangzeb Becomes Mughal Emperor
events.description: After defeating his brothers in a war of succession, Aurangzeb takes the Mughal throne and imprisons his father, Shah Jahan, in Agra Fort. His long reign carries the empire to its greatest size but also strains it through constant warfare and religious conflict.
events.note: User chose 1658 (seizes the throne); the CSV says 1659 (formal coronation). Related: mughal-empire-zenith-aurangzeb (his death).

events.name: Third Battle of Panipat
events.description: The Afghan ruler Ahmad Shah Durrani defeats a large Maratha army at Panipat, in one of the largest and bloodiest battles of its time. The defeat halts Maratha expansion into northern India and leaves a power vacuum that the East India Company later fills.

events.name: Great Bengal Famine
events.description: Drought and crop failure, made far worse by East India Company revenue demands, cause a catastrophic famine in Bengal. Several million people die, by some estimates a third of the population, fuelling criticism of Company rule in Britain.
events.note: Death toll is an estimate (often quoted up to 10 million); the draft avoids a precise figure.

events.name: Lee Surrenders at Appomattox
aliases: end of the American Civil War
events.description: Confederate General Robert E. Lee surrenders the Army of Northern Virginia to Union General Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Court House in Virginia. The surrender effectively ends the American Civil War; five days later President Lincoln is assassinated.

events.name: Amundsen Reaches the South Pole
events.description: The Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen and his team become the first people to reach the South Pole, travelling with skis and sled dogs. Robert Falcon Scott's British party arrives five weeks later and dies on the return journey.
events.note: Region: Antarctica has no legacy label, so Global was used.

events.name: League of Nations Founded
events.description: The League of Nations, created by the peace settlement after the First World War, comes into being with the aim of preventing future wars through collective security. Weakened by the absence of the United States, it fails to stop the aggression that leads to the Second World War.

events.name: Discovery of Pluto
events.description: Clyde Tombaugh at the Lowell Observatory in Arizona discovers Pluto by comparing photographs of the night sky taken days apart. Counted as the ninth planet for decades, it is later reclassified as a dwarf planet.

events.name: Germany Invades the Soviet Union
events.description: Nazi Germany and its allies launch Operation Barbarossa, the largest invasion in history, breaking the pact between Hitler and Stalin. The Eastern Front becomes the deadliest theatre of the Second World War, and Germany's defeat there proves decisive.
events.note: CSV row 235 is also linked to japanese-pearl-harbor.

events.name: Yom Kippur War
events.description: Egypt and Syria launch a surprise attack on Israel on the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur. Israel recovers and pushes back, but the war shakes confidence on both sides, triggers an Arab oil embargo and opens the way to peace between Egypt and Israel.

events.name: Camp David Accords
events.description: Egyptian President Anwar Sadat and Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin, hosted by US President Jimmy Carter, agree a framework for peace at Camp David. It leads to a peace treaty the following year, making Egypt the first Arab state to recognise Israel.

events.name: Gulf War
events.description: A US-led coalition authorised by the United Nations launches Operation Desert Storm to drive Iraqi forces out of Kuwait, which Saddam Hussein had invaded the previous summer. A weeks-long air campaign and a brief ground war liberate Kuwait.
events.note: Year is the war itself (Jan-Feb 1991); the invasion of Kuwait, which the CSV mentions, was in August 1990.

events.name: Bandung Conference
events.description: Leaders of twenty-nine newly independent Asian and African countries, including Nehru, Sukarno, Nasser and Zhou Enlai, meet in Bandung, Indonesia. They call for an end to colonialism and for cooperation outside the Cold War blocs, laying the groundwork for the Non-Aligned Movement.

events.name: Dalai Lama Flees to India
events.description: After a failed Tibetan uprising against Chinese rule in Lhasa, the fourteenth Dalai Lama escapes across the Himalayas to India. He sets up a government in exile at Dharamsala, while Tibet remains under the control of the People's Republic of China.

events.name: Indonesia Proclaims Independence
events.description: Days after Japan's surrender, Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta proclaim the independence of Indonesia from the Netherlands. Four years of armed and diplomatic struggle follow before the Dutch finally recognise the new republic.
events.note: User chose 1945 (proclamation); the CSV says 1949 (Dutch recognition).

events.name: Burma Gains Independence
events.description: Burma becomes independent from Britain as the Union of Burma and chooses to leave the Commonwealth. Its independence leader, Aung San, had been assassinated months earlier, and the new state soon faces ethnic insurgencies and, later, military rule.
events.note: Split from a CSV row that combines Burma and Ceylon (see ceylon-independence).

events.name: Ceylon Gains Independence
events.description: Ceylon becomes independent from Britain as a dominion within the Commonwealth, with D. S. Senanayake as its first prime minister. The island later becomes a republic and takes the name Sri Lanka.
events.note: Split from a CSV row that combines Burma and Ceylon (see burma-independence).

events.name: Assassination of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
events.description: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the founding leader of Bangladesh, is assassinated with most of his family in a military coup in Dhaka. Two of his daughters survive because they are abroad, one of them Sheikh Hasina, who later becomes prime minister.

events.name: Death of Shivaji
events.description: Shivaji, founder of the Maratha kingdom, dies at his hill fort of Raigad. His son Sambhaji succeeds him and continues the long struggle against the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.

events.name: Death of the Buddha
events.description: Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, dies at Kushinagar in northern India at about the age of eighty, an event Buddhists call the parinirvana. His followers soon gather to preserve his teachings, which go on to spread across Asia.
events.note: Approximate and disputed: c. 483 BCE fits the app's birth-of-buddha (-563) plus eighty years, but some scholars date it c. 400 BCE. hippocrates-medicine (-400) could then appear as a defensible DatePick distractor; see doc 11 Phase D.

events.name: John F. Kennedy Elected US President
events.description: John F. Kennedy narrowly defeats Richard Nixon after the first televised presidential debates, becoming the youngest person ever elected US president and the first Catholic. His short presidency spans the Bay of Pigs, the Cuban Missile Crisis and the start of the race to the Moon.

events.name: Ronald Reagan Elected US President
events.description: The former actor and California governor Ronald Reagan defeats Jimmy Carter in a landslide. His presidency brings tax cuts, a military build-up and a harder line against the Soviet Union, followed by arms-control deals with Gorbachev.

events.name: George H. W. Bush Elected US President
events.description: Vice President George H. W. Bush defeats Michael Dukakis to succeed Ronald Reagan. His single term sees the end of the Cold War, the reunification of Germany and the Gulf War.
